name: King of the Ammonites
overview: The King of the Ammonites was a male ruler known primarily for his defeat by King Jotham of Judah, as recorded in 2 Chronicles 27:5. Beyond this military encounter, Scripture does not provide additional details about his tribe or personal background. His role is noted within the context of regional conflicts during the reign of Jotham.
namesAndTitles: The title 'King of the Ammonites' translates to 'king [of the] sons [of] Ammon,' indicating his position as the sovereign leader of the Ammonite people. This designation is a title rather than a personal name and was not given by God, reflecting his earthly authority over Ammon as mentioned in 2 Chronicles 27:5.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture does not record any family relationships for the King of the Ammonites beyond what is noted in his unique attribute of being defeated by King Jotham. There are no additional relational details provided in the biblical text.
scriptureSignificance: The King of the Ammonites is significant in the biblical narrative as an adversary defeated by King Jotham of Judah, illustrating God's providential protection over His people through their leaders. This defeat underscores the challenges faced by Judah from neighboring nations and highlights the faithfulness of God in granting victory to His anointed king. His mention, though brief, serves to confirm the historical realities of inter-kingdom conflicts during this period.
